sprint.name: Clerk Identity Shadow Integration
sprint.classification: B — Identity Contract Integrated; Live Deployment Verification Required
sprint.scope: Official server-only Clerk identity mapping and inactive fail-closed orchestration into the existing Alpha disclosure producer.

evidence.claimBoundary: Twenty-eight deterministic mapping, denial, ordering, isolation, and active-file noninterference checks.
Server-only official Clerk auth adapter; no route, middleware, provider, access policy, or deployment activation.
Deterministic normalization and fail-closed orchestration into the existing Alpha producer.
Architecture, deployment boundary, Scorecard interpretation, missing capabilities, rollback, and next recommendation.
Existing sixty-one-check disclosure-producer and inactive delivery-chain regression.
Point-in-time npm audit inventory, installed dependency tree, bounded reachability assessment, remediation posture, and activation blocker.

scorecard.rationale: Identity verification does not create, rank, revise, or persist organizational cognition.
The shadow is inactive and no real-user comprehension or decision outcome was measured.
No collaboration, contribution, membership, role, or shared-learning behavior changed.
The shadow replaces benchmark-created identity at the production boundary with official server verification and fails closed before access or Runtime.
The official SDK boundary is isolated from deterministic normalization, Discovery policy, Runtime, and product code.

architecture.observation: Clerk server auth supplies identity while Discovery remains the access and disclosure policy owner.
Authentication failure skips access and Runtime; missing access skips Runtime; active access loads once.
Middleware, layout, routes, components, and active product behavior remain unchanged.

benchmarks.summary: Official server identity mapping and fail-closed inactive orchestration are deterministic and isolated.
The existing Alpha policy and disclosure chain remain passing.

researchObservations.observation: No research adapter, Local Understanding Utility profile, nonlinear cognition, or research conclusion changed.

introduced: One official Clerk dependency compatible with the existing framework versions.
One isolated server adapter and one deterministic normalization/orchestration module.
One focused twenty-eight-check validator and one DEPS measurement source.
complexity.justification: The additions replace benchmark-only identity construction at the server boundary without coupling Clerk to Discovery authorization, Runtime, or product behavior.

governanceObservations.observation: Consumer identity now has an official server-verification owner and cannot be supplied by client input or the Alpha password.

sustainabilityObservations.observation: SDK-specific work is replaceable at one server boundary; deterministic policy validation remains provider-independent.

regressions.observation: The integration is inactive and active application files remain byte-equivalent.
The identity boundary does not mutate Runtime and denied paths cannot load it.

unknownsAndUnmeasured.reason: No provider credentials, middleware activation, deployed session, or browser verification was authorized.
The existing access reader and audit boundaries remain injected and non-durable.
The point-in-time audit reports 17 high and 2 critical vulnerable package entries. No remediation or post-remediation validation was performed.

remainingRisks.nextBlockingDependency: Durable Discovery-owned Alpha access and bounded audit storage plus Clerk and Next dependency remediation remain required before activation review.
remainingRisks.remainingDiscoveryPhase: Phase 8 shadows remain inactive; broader Phase 5 Governance and Phase 6 remain paused.
remainingRisks.remainingBenchmarkGap: Live provider-session verification, dependency remediation, durable lifecycle, browser isolation, operational failure handling, and activation rollback remain unmeasured.

rollback.description: Remove the dependency, server adapter, deterministic identity module, validator, command, DEPS source/report, and documentation synchronization; active product and Runtime remain unchanged.

engineeringDecision.rationale: Accept the inactive identity integration as Classification B. Preserve route inactivity and proceed only through a separately authorized durable access and audit storage sprint.
